protections: P1 libtiff tag marshalling: before a tag reaches TIFFSetField, the encoder gives it a TIFF type (explicit tagtype, else enum-range checked, else autodetected from the Python value) and routes variable-length shapes through a registered custom field (src/encode.c:741-798; src/PIL/TiffImagePlugin.py:1587-1624).

P2 core-tag withholding: tags whose array length is fixed or derived from other tags are kept out of the libtiff encoder by a denylist so libtiff never receives a caller-sized array for them (src/PIL/TiffImagePlugin.py:1560-1571, 1601).

P3 libtiff bridge sizing: the decoder sizes its buffer from the TIFF tags and refuses strips/tiles whose libtiff-reported size exceeds that buffer (src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c:365-389, 446-465), and the client I/O procs are meant to copy at most the declared buffer bytes (src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c:50-92).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: the documented and tested route for a BYTE/UNDEFINED tag passes a bytes object, so a non-bytes value looks like caller error rather than an input vector
core tags are Pillow's own business and the denylist already removes the ones that segfault, so a caller-supplied core tag is treated as out of scope
re-saving the tags of a loaded TIFF is normal ('save(load(x))') and blocking more tags would break round-trips, so the six-entry denylist is assumed complete

the declared type comes from the same IFD the caller already controls, so trusting it looks equivalent to trusting the value, and the TIFF_BYTE..TIFF_DOUBLE range check at encode.c:745 appears to make it safe
libtiff is assumed to validate strip/tile offsets before it seeks and reads, so the client procs are assumed never to see a position past EOF and never to compute a negative count
the TIFFStripSize comparison two blocks later aborts before any data is copied, so the missing multiply guard in the strip path looks harmless

masking: T1 is masked on the ordinary path by the str->bytes conversion at src/PIL/TiffImagePlugin.py:1602-1603, so only values that survive as int/bytes/tuple reach the shape mismatch in the C marshaller

T6 is masked by the TIFFStripSize abort at src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c:457; removing or weakening that comparison (for example by sizing the buffer from Pillow's own bits instead of the libtiff report) would expose the missing multiply guard at src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c:444

conflicts.what: the natural T1 rule (BYTE/UNDEFINED values must be bytes and array lengths must match a declared count) also rejects the tuple-valued core arrays that the dpi/resolution/own-tag path feeds through the same atts loop (src/PIL/TiffImagePlugin.py:1487-1515), so the two groups need opposite scoping

blocking all core tags closes T2 but removes PLANAR_CONFIGURATION, BITSPERSAMPLE, SAMPLESPERPIXEL and dpi tags that Pillow itself writes (src/PIL/TiffImagePlugin.py:1449, 1502-1515), which are must-keep-working

fairness_risks: Must-keep-working: saving a loaded TIFF must round-trip its tags (src/PIL/TiffImagePlugin.py:1582-1584); a rule that refuses all file-sourced metadata contradicts 'save(load(x)) == x'.

Must-keep-working: BYTE arrays are documented as bytes objects while tuples were the previous accepted shape (Tests/test_file_libtiff.py:272-275); a hard 'must be bytes' rule breaks that backwards compatibility.

Must-keep-working: dpi/resolution/description/software are core tags written through the same atts loop (src/PIL/TiffImagePlugin.py:1487-1506), so a blanket core-tag refusal contradicts a legitimate feature.
Refused input shape: array-valued custom tags of arbitrary length are a legitimate use exercised by Tests/test_file_libtiff.py:261-271; a fixed-length security rule would reject them.

design.why: The five traps sit on one operation (libtiff tag marshalling) but need four different judgements: T1 is a value-shape rule only for BYTE/UNDEFINED, T4 is a rule about trusting the declared type from the IFD, T2/T3 are a rule about core tags and the denylist, and T5 is a completely separate client-proc bound on the read side. They carry different reasons to dismiss (caller error, Pillow's own tags, legitimate round-trip, libtiff self-validation), the deepseek bait is T2/T5 (protection never existed, and a plausible argument that libtiff/denylist already handles it), and the mimo bait is T1/T4 (a value shape coupled to a type, and a type taken from a caller-supplied identity field). The two must-keep-working conflicts (tuple BYTE arrays and Pillow's own core tags) force the solver to scope each guard instead of applying one broad rule.

unverified: A/B identity: the pinned tree is pre-8.1.0 (src/PIL/_version.py:2) and contains the two security fixes documented at docs/releasenotes/8.1.0.rst:44-48; which of those two is CVE-2020-35654 is inferred from the candidate summary and the two-commit b_fix, not read from the advisory text.

The GIF route was checked and rejected for this analysis: the in-tree GIF fix is the xsize==1 read guard at src/libImaging/GifEncode.c:236-242 and no reachable out-of-bounds write was found in the encoder, so the TIFF metadata route was used.
Whether the later fix is the C-side value check (T1) or a Python-side tag filter (T3/T4) could not be determined from the pinned code; both are recorded as separate groups.

libtiff's exact TIFFVSetField/TIFFCheckMalloc behaviour for a negative or mismatched count is version-dependent and the library is not part of this repository; T1/T2 could therefore end in an error return rather than a write for a particular libtiff version.
Whether libtiff itself rejects strip/tile offsets beyond EOF before calling the client seek/read procs (T5 reachability) is outside this repository.
The candidate record's claim that GHSA-57h3-9rgr-c24m is an incomplete fix of CVE-2020-35654 could not be confirmed from the pinned tree; only the code-level gaps listed above are verified.
